references.text: The same principle of offering two turtledoves or two young pigeons when one cannot afford a lamb, used in connection with the guilt offering.
Additional provision for an alternative sacrifice for those who cannot afford it, showing God's care for the poor.
Similar provision for cleansing from leprosy where two turtledoves or two young pigeons are used as an alternative for the one who cannot afford a lamb.
Clarification of how the two birds are to be used—one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering, following the same pattern as in 12:8.
Basic instruction on using turtledoves or young pigeons as a burnt offering.
Mary and Joseph offered a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons at Jesus' presentation in the temple, showing that they followed the provision for those who could not afford a lamb.
